NOTE:
Born in Tokyo in 1916, Pang Tseng-Ying grew up in Beijing, where he studied calligraphy under his mother and received training in traditional Chinese painting from an early age. At 18, he entered Jinghua College of Art, specializing in Western painting, and later pursued further studies in Japan at Nihon University. After graduation, he returned to teach in Beijing. He relocated to Taiwan in 1949, teaching at Taipei First Girls High School, National Taiwan College of Arts, and Fu-Hsin Trade & Arts School. His first solo exhibition, held at Argent Gallery, New York in 1954, brought him international recognition and laid the foundation for his later career in the United States. A key participant in Taiwan’s modern art movement of the 1950s–60s, he received the Chiang Kai-shek Award in 1965 and moved to the U.S. in 1966.
Pang’s artistic philosophy emphasizes that painting must unite creation with truth, sensibility, and reality. His early oils reveal a surrealist tendency, employing brushing, smearing, dripping, and flowing techniques to form dynamic abstract compositions. His richly decorative bird-and-flower paintings, inspired by Five Dynasties aesthetics as well as embroidery and textile traditions, are marked by vibrant color and intricate patterning. His watercolors integrate Western realism with the subtle, philosophical qualities of Chinese ink painting.
Selected exhibitions: 1954 Argent Gallery, New York; 1961 Chi Hsiang Studio First Exhibition, Taipei; 1967 Church Center for the United Nations, New York; 1983 National Museum of History, Taipei; 1987 St. John’s University Gallery, New York; 1997 Taipei Gallery, New York; 2000, 2006 Lin & Keng Gallery, Taipei.

FURTHER DETAILS






Singaporean collector Mr. Tan Sin Liou (1922-1992) had familial ties to Fujian, China. His grandfather immigrated to Singapore, where he operated a palm tree business, later also became the owner of the Supreme House in the city’s commercial district. Apart from his entrepreneurial pursuits, Mr. Tan held a keen interest in traditional Chinese culture, as evidenced by his collection of Chinese calligraphy, paintings, and folding fans. Since the 1960s, numerous painters such as Zhao Shao’ang, Yang Shanshen, Guan Shanyue, Li Xiongcai, and Rong Shushi showcased their works in Singapore due to its proximity to China. Mr. Tan, recognized for his generosity and hospitality towards these artists, notably fostered a close relationship with Yang Shanshen.

The celebrated Canton Collection belonged to Hong Kong collector and architect Ronald Poon (1942–2022). Poon came from a distinguished Guangzhou family of merchants and art collectors who settled in the city in the late 18th century. His ancestor Pan Zhengwei founded the Ting Fan Lou Collection, one of southern China’s most important Qing dynasty painting collections. Inheriting part of this legacy, Poon grew up surrounded by art and culture. As an active member and former chairman of the Min Chiu Society, he also helped organise major exhibitions of Chinese paintings in Hong Kong and abroad.
Poon renamed his family collection Xiao Ting Fan Lou, or the Canton Collection, and expanded it with contemporary Chinese paintings by leading 20th century artists he knew personally, including Zhu Qizhan, Huang Zhou, Liu Haisu, and Huang Yongyu. These works reflect his modern aesthetic and create a dynamic dialogue with his classical masterpieces.

Sun Ah Book Center opened its doors in 1968 and has provided a trading platform for Hong Kong and overseas scholars of literature, history and philosophy for over half a century. In addition to operating two bookstores, the Center organized many large-scale events in the past, including twenty-six antique books auctions, the “1930s Out-of-Print Antique Book Fair”, and the “Shenzhen National College Foreign Edition Literature and History Book Fair”.
With the enthusiastic effort of its founder Tsang Sook Yin and her son Dr So Keng Chit, Sun Ah Book Center is warmly welcomed by the book and manuscript collectors community. The Center sold countless ancient books of Ming and Qing Dynasties, and manuscripts of Shen Congwen, Zhou Zuoren, Albert Einstein, Zhang Ailing, Hu Shi and other celebrities. Its supply sources include Tokyo, Florence, and many North American cities. Over the past few decades, as the owners acquired books and manuscripts from collectors for their business, they, in turn, began to collect paintings and calligraphy to form the collection of Classical and Modern works as we present to you now.

Principal Madam Chua Liang, a native of Chao’an County, Guangdong Province, China, was born in Shantou City. Jiang Tingfu (Tsiang Tingfu, 1895–1965) was a renowned Chinese historian, educator, and diplomat from Shaoyang, Hunan. He studied in the United States, attending Oberlin College before earning a doctorate in history from Columbia University. Upon returning to China, he taught at Nankai University and Tsinghua University, where he helped introduce modern historical methods and became a leading scholar of modern Chinese history. His influential work Chinese Modern History reshaped understanding of China’s encounter with the modern world.
During the Sino-Japanese War, Jiang entered public service and diplomacy, holding positions such as Director of Political Affairs in the Executive Yuan, Ambassador to the Soviet Union, and China’s representative to the United Nations. Combining scholarly rigor with diplomatic experience, he played an important role in both intellectual and international affairs. His broad global perspective and pioneering contributions to historical scholarship secured his place among the most influential Chinese intellectuals of the twentieth century.
